request.text:
Create eight markdown files in the repository: docs/n01.md, docs/n02.md, docs/n03.md, docs/n04.md,
docs/n05.md, docs/n06.md, docs/n07.md and docs/n08.md.
Create them strictly one at a time, in that order, and write each file completely before you start
the next one. Each file must have exactly three lines:
line 1 the markdown title "# Note NN" for its own number NN,
line 2 the line "Status: reviewed",
line 3 one short sentence of your own about note NN.
Do not create any other file and do not create them in a single batch.

writeObservation.note: The runtime enforces a write boundary (write_containment "verified"), so a write outside the granted paths would have been refused whether or not it was reported; every entry is a write the codex runtime itself reported through a tool event; the coordinator does not watch the filesystem, so this list can only be as complete as the runtime's reporting. An empty list therefore means no such write succeeded.

evidence.note: acceptance is decided from verifier-executed check receipts, the integrity of the fixtures those receipts executed, and the run-level blockers listed under acceptance.reasons; the runtime-reported fields above are context, not evidence of correctness

containment.writeContainmentNote: workspace-write with explicit writableRoots plus excludeSlashTmp and excludeTmpdirEnvVar: writes inside the granted root succeed while writes to a sibling workspace, to /tmp and to $TMPDIR are denied, network is denied, and read-only denies every write. Checked both through command/exec and through a model-driven turn asked to write outside its workspace

evidence.containmentNote: Write confinement for this run is what the codex adapter reports as write_containment "verified" (established against 0.147.0 on darwin): workspace-write with explicit writableRoots plus excludeSlashTmp and excludeTmpdirEnvVar: writes inside the granted root succeed while writes to a sibling workspace, to /tmp and to $TMPDIR are denied, network is denied, and read-only denies every write. Checked both through command/exec and through a model-driven turn asked to write outside its workspace Any write seen outside the granted paths is listed above and blocks acceptance. The candidate workspace is a linked Git worktree: development isolation, not a security sandbox. Neither installed runtime confines reads at all — a worker can read files outside the repository, and this run did not prevent that. Each check ran in a separate disposable copy of the frozen candidate under a sanitized environment, with that copy, its HOME and its TMPDIR placed outside the coordinator state root, so no relative path from a check reaches coordinator state; the state root is fingerprinted on both sides of each check window, so a write that reached it by absolute path is recorded as an integrity failure instead of passing silently. Each receipt's `containment` and `stateRootGuard` report what was actually placed and actually measured. That is placement and detection, not confinement: repository test code still runs with this user's own filesystem privileges and can name any absolute path, so it can still read or write anything this user can — the home directory and the registered project checkout included — and an in-place overwrite that does not change a file's identity is recorded as an observation rather than a violation. An enforced execution boundary for tool and test subprocesses (FR042) is an R1 gate and is not claimed here; acceptance compensates only by refusing evidence whose fixtures the candidate changed.
